assessment: The ten answer the diagnosis's two measured weaknesses and the deck's stated direction. Three picks move black mana, the binding axis (27/36 sources, 76.4% on-curve). One closes the single uncovered interaction class, the graveyard. The rest deepen the token-to-damage engine: two-card infinite halves that pair with Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Vito and Sanguine Bond, plus trigger doublers and width payoffs that scale with eminence tokens. One famous card deliberately absent: Rest in Peace would cover the graveyard class, but under it creatures exile instead of dying, so Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant and Cordial Vampire never trigger — the cheap answer that blanks your own drain suite is not an answer.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite lifeloss (each opponent's life to zero, one at a time)

cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose

ten.closes: THE SURVIVING INFINITE (stacks 004 and 006): Bloodthirsty Conqueror + a lifegain-loss half
ten.why: The infinite plan currently rests on one 7.1%-of-openers body; with Vito, Sanguine Bond and Bloodthirsty Conqueror all in the 99, this single enchantment makes it four two-card pairings, and stacks 001 and 005 are checker-passed resolutions of both of its loops.
ten.unlocks: Any drain trigger — a Sanctum Seeker attack, one Blood Artist death — becomes a game-ending loop the moment the second half is on the battlefield.

ten.why: The one land swap that gains a black source with red and white unchanged — Battlefield Forge out — and with 24 of the deck's 29 creatures sharing Edgar's Vampire type it scries on most creature casts; sized honestly, it closes 1 of the 9-source black gap.
ten.unlocks: A fourth tapland (cap is eight, aggro runs near zero — three is still comfortable) that smooths every eminence turn instead of just fixing one.

ten.why: A three-mana Vampire — eminence fuel — that turns every lifegain event into 1 life from each opponent: a Sanctum Seeker swing or a Blood Artist death now hits the whole table, and it forms a second two-card loop with Bloodthirsty Conqueror.
ten.unlocks: A gain-to-loss half on a typal body, so the drain web no longer routes exclusively through Vito and Sanguine Bond.

ten.why: Graveyard is the one interaction class the deck answers zero times — confirmed at the oracle level — and this is the one-mana answer the breadth measure actually credits (hate:graveyard), where a Bojuka Bog-style utility land carries only land tags and moves nothing.
ten.unlocks: A line against reanimator and Yawgmoth-style tables: surgical exile on entry, whole-graveyard exile on demand, and a cantrip when nobody is playing that game.

ten.why: Name Vampire and the triggered abilities of Sanctum Seeker, Cordial Vampire, Champion of Dusk, Vampire Socialite and Blood Artist each trigger an additional time — on a colorless ward-{2} body the 27/36 black shortage never taxes.
ten.unlocks: Sanctum Seeker attacks drain twice per Vampire; one caution before counting tokens: whether it interacts with the command-zone eminence trigger at all needs a stack scenario — the ability doubles triggers of creatures you control, and a commander in the command zone is not one.

ten.why: Every token created — the eminence 1/1 on each Vampire cast, Bloodline Keeper activations, and every extra body Anointed Procession, Mondrak or Ocelot Pride adds — costs each opponent 1 life on creation; the audit's closer search ranks it the top pool card joining the drain component.
ten.unlocks: A flying converter that pays off token-MAKING rather than token combat — Impact Tremors redundancy that gets multiplied by the doublers instead of merely counting entries.

ten.why: The deck's 13 wincon copies mostly cash out in the attack step, and Isshin doubles that step: Sanctum Seeker's per-Vampire drain, Drana's counters and Minas Tirith's draw each trigger an additional time on every swing — for {1}{R}{W}, costing nothing in the strained colour.
ten.unlocks: Attack-trigger doubling that turns a five-Vampire alpha strike into ten Sanctum Seeker drains before damage.

ten.why: A Sanguine Bond that dies into itself — when killed as a creature it returns as an enchantment — so the gain-to-loss half survives exactly the sweeper a go-wide deck fears, and it pairs with Bloodthirsty Conqueror for another two-card loop; read the card: it drains one TARGET opponent, not each.
ten.unlocks: Wipe-resilient redundancy for the Sanguine Bond seat, which stack 006's lethal currently depends on.

ten.why: The second black swap after Path of Ancestry: replacing the single Plains keeps white at 21 sources and adds a 28th black one, untapped whenever a Plains or Swamp is down — Godless Shrine and Savai Triome both satisfy it — at the real cost that Prismatic Vista then fetches only Swamps.
ten.unlocks: Progress on the binding axis by the only levers it has — the diagnosis prices the gap at 9 sources and no single-card cut re-prices it, so each credited land is a point of on-curve castability for the double-black drain quorum.

ten.why: Five eminence tokens entering means five +1/+1 counters on every Vampire you control — width converts directly into mass pump, and the counters stay when a lord is shot, the same resilience argument the counters half of the combat plan already makes.
ten.unlocks: A payoff that scales with the number of tokens made per turn, which is the exact dimension Anointed Procession, Mondrak and Elspeth already multiply; the cost is real trigger bookkeeping on a five-mana double-white enchantment.

gaps: The Bloodletter of Aclazotz drain-doubler line has zero pool closers — the audit's combo and role routes both return empty — so nothing on this list backs it up; a functional cousin (life-loss doubling on another body) could not be grounded in any index channel.

Whether the second fixing swap (Isolated Chapel for Plains) pays for itself is a goldfish question the diagnosis leaves open: black remains 8 sources short after Path of Ancestry, and only a seed-matched sandbox can price swap number two.

Roaming Throne's non-interaction with the command-zone eminence trigger is a rules read, not a verified fact — a stack scenario should settle it before any pilot counts on (or writes off) doubled tokens.

No candidate_pool.json exists for this deck, so the ten were scouted from the audit's closer search, the combo/synergy/obsolescence indexes and the colour-identity-filtered pool, not from a scored pool.

Whether Exquisite Blood's slot is best spent here at all is the diagnosis's open cross-deck question; this list ranks it on this deck's evidence alone and the orchestrator holds the allocation decision.
